title: AI Is Rewriting the Rules of the Consumer Journey in Asia
gist: Using BCG's Global Consumer Radar survey of almost 5,500 consumers in China, India, Japan and South Korea, BCG finds LLM search reaches only 12% of Asian purchase journeys but 64% of its users say it shaped their brand choice, tying it for the second-highest influence behind social media. Contrary to the incumbent-concentration assumption, LLM search widens consideration sets, and with Asia-Pacific CMOs prioritizing agentic commerce more than peers in North America and Europe, BCG urges brands to invest ahead of reach via GEO, machine-readable data and agent-ready checkout.

insights.claim: BCG separates marketing touchpoints into two metrics: reach (share of purchase journeys in which consumers used a touchpoint) and influence (share of those users who said the touchpoint stood out in shaping the brand they bought), arguing that the interaction between the two, not either alone, should guide marketing budget allocation.
insights.speaker: Parul Bajaj
insights.so_what: A reusable lens for judging ad-channel economics: high-reach/low-influence channels (legacy media, some display) are overpriced relative to low-reach/high-influence ones (LLM search).

insights.claim: Across China, India, Japan and South Korea, which channels consumers use differs sharply by market, but how much a channel matters once used differs far less — influence is far more stable across markets than reach.
insights.speaker: Parul Bajaj
insights.so_what: Influence rates observed in early-adopter markets can be used to forecast channel value in lagging markets once adoption catches up — a template for sizing LLM-search ad/commerce TAM in Japan and Korea.
insights.quote: which channels consumers use differs sharply by market, but how much a channel matters once it’s used differs far less

insights.claim: Nearly half of Asian consumers are undecided on brand at the start of a purchase journey, meaning brand preference is increasingly formed during the journey rather than before it, and the highest-reach channels are all digital.
insights.speaker: Parul Bajaj
insights.so_what: Erodes the value of pre-built brand equity for Asian consumer brands and raises the value of in-journey digital presence — favors platforms that own the decision moment.
insights.quote: Brand preference is no longer set before the journey begins; it’s formed during it.

insights.claim: The BCG analysis draws on almost 5,500 consumers across China, India, Japan and South Korea from its 14-market Global Consumer Radar survey, covering 16 product categories ranging from packaged snacks to cars.
insights.speaker: Parul Bajaj
insights.so_what: Sample breadth across low- and high-involvement categories makes the LLM-influence finding more than a tech-gadget artifact, though category-level splits are not disclosed.

themes.theme: Social commerce dominance in China and India

insights.claim: Social media reaches consumers in 21% of purchase journeys across Asia versus an average of 14% elsewhere in the world, with reach of 31% in China and 29% in India but only 12% in Japan and 14% in South Korea, where internet research is the top reach channel.
insights.speaker: Parul Bajaj
insights.so_what: Social-platform ad and commerce monetization in Asia is concentrated in China and India; Japan and Korea remain search-led markets where search incumbents retain the discovery moment.

insights.claim: In China, social media has moved beyond discovery to become commerce infrastructure itself, with livestream shopping, influencer-curated product lists and in-app shoppable links letting consumers go from inspiration to purchase without leaving the platform.
insights.speaker: Parul Bajaj
insights.so_what: Closed-loop social commerce captures both ad and transaction economics — the benchmark model for what integrated platforms elsewhere are chasing.
insights.quote: social media has evolved well beyond discovery to become part of the commerce infrastructure itself

insights.claim: India is following China toward social commerce, driven by rapid growth of the creator economy and deeper links between leading social/video platforms and e-commerce marketplaces that connect creator-led discovery directly with purchase.
insights.speaker: Parul Bajaj
insights.so_what: Watch Indian social-to-marketplace integrations and creator-commerce monetization as the next large social-commerce growth pocket after China.

themes.theme: LLM search punching above its reach

insights.claim: LLM search already reaches 12% of purchase journeys across China, India, Japan and South Korea, placing it among the region's top five touchpoints by reach, ahead of TV and radio, print and billboards.
insights.speaker: Parul Bajaj
insights.so_what: LLM assistants have already overtaken legacy media as a purchase-discovery channel in Asia — a direct share threat to traditional ad budgets.

insights.claim: Only 12% of Asian purchase journeys involve LLM search, yet 64% of consumers who use it say it shaped their brand choice, tying LLM search for the second-highest influence of any touchpoint in Asia, just behind social media.
insights.speaker: Parul Bajaj
insights.so_what: Per-use conversion power of AI assistants is already near the top of the stack; as usage scales, the value of being cited by LLMs compounds — bullish for platforms that monetize AI answer surfaces.
insights.quote: fully 64% of the consumers who use it say that it shapes their brand choices

insights.claim: LLM search reach varies more across Asian markets than almost any other touchpoint — roughly 22-23% of purchase journeys in India versus 5-6% in Japan, more than a fourfold gap — while its influence among users stays in a tight band of roughly 52% to 68% across all four markets.
insights.speaker: Parul Bajaj
insights.so_what: India is the leading AI-assisted-shopping market in the region; Japan is the laggard with the most headroom — adoption, not efficacy, is the swing variable.

insights.claim: Brands should not wait for LLM search reach to scale before investing, because its influence is likely to hold at similarly strong levels as adoption grows; optimizing purely for reach risks under-investing in a channel already punching above its weight.
insights.speaker: Parul Bajaj
insights.so_what: Implies early budget migration toward LLM visibility/GEO ahead of measurable reach — a leading demand signal for GEO tooling and AI-answer ad products.
insights.quote: Optimizing purely for reach risks under-investing in a channel that’s already punching above its weight.

themes.theme: LLMs widen, not concentrate, brand consideration

insights.claim: Contrary to marketers' assumption that LLM search would concentrate influence around a handful of large incumbent brands, in more than half of LLM-assisted purchase journeys consumers end up considering brands they would not otherwise have found.
insights.speaker: Parul Bajaj
insights.so_what: AI discovery weakens scale-based brand moats built on broad reach advertising — a risk to incumbent consumer brands' pricing power and an opening for challengers.
insights.quote: So far, marketers have assumed that LLM search will concentrate influence around a handful of large incumbents. But as our recent report on consumer behavior shows, the opposite is happening.

insights.claim: Because LLM search can surface brands with low reach through traditional touchpoints, winning the purchase journey no longer depends solely on investing across reach channels before the consumer turns to an LLM — the LLM itself becomes a route into the shortlist.
insights.speaker: Parul Bajaj
insights.so_what: Lowers the customer-acquisition barrier for smaller brands and reduces the returns on mass-reach media spend — negative for traditional media ad pools over time.

insights.claim: LLM search has rapidly become a trusted consumer source because it cuts through a cluttered, option-crowded marketplace with personalized, direct and transparent recommendations that feel relevant to individual needs.
insights.speaker: Parul Bajaj
insights.so_what: Trust is the precondition for handing over transactions — the trajectory to monitor is whether trust survives the introduction of sponsored placements in AI answers.

insights.claim: 28% of Asia-Pacific CMOs rank agentic commerce among their top three priorities, versus 23% of CMOs in North America and 13% in Europe, and BCG says the shift from LLMs shaping the shortlist to LLMs initiating transactions is no longer a distant scenario.
insights.speaker: Parul Bajaj
insights.so_what: Asia-Pacific is positioned as the lead market for agent-completed purchases; Europe lags badly — expect agentic checkout volumes and vendor wins to show first in APAC.

insights.claim: Brands should structure product, pricing and availability data so outside AI commerce agents can discover, price and complete purchases directly, while tracking multiple emerging agentic checkout standards such as ChatGPT's Instant Checkout and Amazon's 'Buy for Me' rather than building around just one.
insights.speaker: Parul Bajaj
insights.so_what: Agentic checkout standards remain unsettled — a live platform battle between OpenAI and Amazon for the transaction layer; product-data/feed-management vendors benefit regardless of winner.

insights.claim: BCG recommends measuring marketing outcomes with AI agents, not just people, by tracking share of mentions, citations and recommendation rates, and asks leadership whether they would want their own agent to be the one closing a consumer's purchase.
insights.speaker: Parul Bajaj
insights.so_what: New KPI category (AI share-of-voice) is emerging — a budget line that will fund AI-visibility analytics tools.

insights.claim: LLM search draws heavily on sources beyond brand-owned websites — forums, review sites, social content and Wikipedia — so brand discoverability in AI answers depends on managing the brand's broader digital presence through generative engine optimization (GEO).
insights.speaker: Parul Bajaj
insights.so_what: Third-party content hubs (reviews, forums, Wikipedia) gain strategic value as LLM citation sources — raising the value of UGC platforms whose content feeds AI answers.
insights.locator: Win in LLM Search and Other LLM Answer Modes

insights.claim: BCG's GEO playbook: reverse-engineer LLM answers for key category queries to see which sources are cited and where the brand is absent; rewrite content for machines using question-style phrasing, schema markup, clear subheadings and comparison tables; and monitor citation frequency, LLM sentiment on product attributes and citation staleness as a test-and-learn program.
insights.speaker: Parul Bajaj
insights.so_what: Defines the concrete scope of a GEO services/software market analogous to early SEO — a consulting and tooling spend category forming now.
insights.locator: Win in LLM Search and Other LLM Answer Modes

insights.claim: Ownership of AI discoverability should move out of a single SEO or marketing team into shared accountability across marketing, product and technology with a named owner and clear decision rights, treating LLM search, agentic commerce and data foundations as one connected system because a gap in any one undercuts the others.
insights.speaker: Parul Bajaj
insights.so_what: Signals that AI-commerce readiness is becoming a cross-functional, CTO-involved spend rather than a marketing line item — larger deal sizes for enterprise data/commerce vendors.
insights.locator: Establish the Foundations for LLM Search and Agentic Commerce

insights.claim: Social media, internet research, LLM search, brand websites and LLM agents feed on each other and are converging into a single connected system, so managing them as isolated channels leads to missed influence.
insights.speaker: Parul Bajaj
insights.so_what: Channel-siloed ad-tech and agency models are exposed; integrated platforms spanning discovery, answers and checkout gain.
insights.quote: treating them as isolated levers is a recipe for missed influence
